questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Weather, courses in English, food and culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: You don't really get any information from the university before going. Once the semester starts they will send you some emails, you just need to figure out stuff when you get there.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Emails, you can contact the Erasmus coordinator Massimo Costa.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Almost no information, but it worked out fine and they are generally very flexible with Erasmus students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty hard to find something, we used Spotahome which worked out fine, but the rent is generally very expensive in Milan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's expensive! If you want to save some money maybe try to find something around Citta Studi or Aquabella - it's still pretty close to the city center but a bit more affordable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register online in Unimia, super easy. It was harder to find information about the courses and their schedules, some of which was only posted right before the semester began. You can change your registrations for a while so you can try out different courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the Erasmus coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Everyone gets the courses they want is my experience. I got every course I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's hard to figure out the schedule because the courses overlap and you need to take a lot of course to get 30 ECTS. So check all the schedules and make an excel sheet or something. Try out different courses - you can change your choices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was very different from course to course, some were super easy and some a bit harder, but the level was generally lower than UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are not many required readings so it's more about listening to the teacher and taking notes. Some teachers require participation and do cold calls.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Climate Change and Energy Law
Legal Clinic on Arctic Studies
Public Administration for Sustainable Development
Sustainable Transport: Legal Issues
Comparative Contract Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: 'International Climate Change and Energy Law' was very interesting and a bit more challenging than other courses. Also 'Sustainable Transport: Legal Issues' was a very interesting topic and the teacher interacts a lot with the students.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It's expensive to get into clubs in Milan.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The regional trains are super cheap, you can get to Lago di Como for 5 euros. And you don't need to buy any books for uni. Also drinks and food are pretty cheap when you eat out, but supermarkets are just as expensive as Copenhagen if not more.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a sports union (CUS) where you can sign up to do a lot of different sports. CUS also have ski trips which I participated in and enjoyed very much! Otherwise, there does not seem to be many activities which are inclusive towards exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The ski trips and maybe join a sport through CUS. Also, ESN (Erasmus Student Network) arranges a welcome night before the semester begins - go to that, it's where I met all my friends.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel! Lago di Como is so close and has the most beautiful hikes (can recommend Mandello del Lario for hiking). I also really liked Turin which is also close by. There are so many beautiful places in Italy and Milan is very well connected by train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to take courses with Italian students (not just Erasmus students) and talk to them there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Italians often don't like to speak English even though a lot of them are better at it than they say.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Aperitivo (going out to drinks before dinner)! And Italians are mostly really nice and helpful if you want to practice Italian.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: You get almost no information, but don't stress - you will figure it out once you get there. Try to get a good course schedule so you have some days off to do one-day trips. And just relax and enjoy amazing Milan!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people from different countries and traveling around beautiful Italy.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was a bit stressful to figure out everything with the courses in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
